items.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I had him on the show. He did a wonderful show.

ctx.x: He was a trumpet . . . that’s a whole other story, I guess.

But he was a wonderful guest. He was just a wonderful man. I was really happy to have him and found out . . . he told me so much about his life with his father. Oh, so many of them. Even people that you don’t . . . that really aren’t that well known, like, for instance, Roy Kral. I had him on the show. He did a wonderful show. And George Shearing. It’s always a pleasure to have somebody again that you know is going to not drop the ball, because a lot of times this does happen. Somebody gets nervous. But then the…

What do you consider that makes it a good interview? What do you, what makes that easy to interview these people? What is it? Is it any particular element or thing? Is it because of their relaxation? Or is the rapport?

items.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: Marian McPartland took us, we were sitting backstage talking

ctx.x: She had such a marvelous instrument and she had such facility with it, and she always did good music and had good groups, so I mean she’s a-okay, and always was. But I liked her early stuff, the way she sang, you know, simpler.

I just remembered that last night, Marian McPartland took us, we were sitting backstage talking, and she took us back to Jump Town, where met and started playing. She said that she and Jimmy McPartland were playing in Chicago.
